newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Abu Dhabi sets up $136 million leasing company.
newsitem.headline: Abu Dhabi sets up $136 million leasing company.

text.p: Abu Dhabi emirate in the United Arab Emirates on Sunday issued a decree setting up a $136 million leasing company, the latest in a string of new issues in the oil-rich Gulf Arab state.
The decree, carried by the official WAM news agency, said the new company -- al-Waha International Leasing Company -- would have a capital of 500 million dirhams ($136 million).
It said the company -- which will own, manage, sell and lease a variety of assets -- will issue 50 million shares with a nominal value of 10 dirhams each.
The decree did not name the founders nor say when subscription would open. It gave no other details.
The UAE -- a federation of seven emirates led by Abu Dhabi and Dubai -- is trying to diversify its oil-dependent and state-dominated economy and give the private sector a bigger role.

Abu Dhabi on Wednesday announced it was setting up the Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank with a capital of one billion dirhams, in which the Abu Dhabi government would own 10 percent, the president's private office 50 million dirhams and the founders -- who it did not name -- 240 million dirhams.
The rest would be offered to UAE nationals and the shares would have a nominal value of 10 dirhams each.
Last month Emaar Properties, in which the Dubai government has a 10 percent stake, was launched. Emaar -- capitalised at one billion dirhams -- was five times overscribed.
